answer: Disk haven: each key must keep its own 200 GB replica of public data, sealed with the key id by a slow, sequential 2-hour encoding. At random times the network asks for Merkle proofs of 10 random 4 KB leaves within 20 s. Resealing takes hours, so only stored bytes pass; keeping 90% passes just 0.9^10, about 35%. Unlike a one-shot puzzle, disk can't be time-shared: 1,000 keys need 200 TB (~$3,000 of drives) versus ~$3 for one honest agent. A quartz-timed deadline, not an ivory-tower registry, does the enforcing.
